evidence.quote: The current policy stance is well positioned to address the risks to both sides of our dual mandate.
For 2026, I have revised up my growth forecast modestly in recent weeks, informed by signs of the economy's continued resilience.
Progress on disinflation has stalled over the past year, and inflation remains elevated relative to our 2 percent target.
Certainly, some upside risks remain, but I expect the disinflationary process to resume this year once increased tariffs pass through more fully to prices.
In this less dynamic labor market, the downside risks to employment remain, but my baseline is for the unemployment rate to hold approximately steady throughout this year.
This implies that there is more leeway for the supply side of the economy to evolve without the need for precautionary monetary policy restraint.
